summary: Will Unwin looks ahead to Manchester United's Champions League trip to Galatasaray, comparing it with the infamous 1993 elimination in Istanbul. A defeat would again end United's European campaign, while a win (if Copenhagen lose to Bayern Munich) would put qualification back in their hands. Former players Gary Pallister and Mike Phelan recall the hostility of 1993 and the lessons learned, and the piece notes United's poor recent Champions League record and the hopes placed on teenagers Garnacho and Mainoo.
one_line: Thirty years after the 1993 'Welcome to Hell' elimination, Manchester United return to Istanbul needing a result against Galatasaray to keep their Champions League hopes alive.
key_facts: In 1993 Manchester United were eliminated by Galatasaray in the second round of the Champions League after a 3-3 first-leg draw at Old Trafford and a goalless second leg in Istanbul.
Eric Cantona was sent off late in the 1993 second leg, and there was a post-match melee in the tunnel involving the United squad and riot police.
United were greeted at the Istanbul airport in 1993 by Galatasaray supporters and the infamous 'Welcome to Hell' banner.
The 1993 tie was United's first return to Europe's top table after an absence of 24 years; much of the squad had won the European Cup Winners' Cup in 1990-91.
A defeat to Galatasaray on Wednesday would end United's Champions League campaign; a win, assuming Copenhagen lose to Bayern Munich, would put qualification back in their hands.

Gary Pallister, injured in 1993, said he never experienced hostility like it in the rest of his career; a bell boy drew a finger across his throat and Brian McClair had a cleaner bang on his bedroom ceiling.
United's last crunch-match win in the Champions League was a 3-1 away win at Paris Saint-Germain in the 2018-19 round of 16 after losing the home leg 2-0.
United lost their final two group games in 2020-21 and were eliminated, and in 2015-16 Wolfsburg won the deciding group match to knock them out.
Galatasaray beat United 3-2 at Old Trafford in early October, with Mauro Icardi scoring the winner.
Six of United's 1993 squad went on to win the Champions League six years later; Mike Phelan said the experience 'did galvanise us'.
Erik ten Hag is missing key players for the trip to Istanbul.
In the win against Everton on Sunday, Alejandro Garnacho scored an overhead kick and Kobbie Mainoo impressed on his full Premier League debut, possibly earning a start in Turkey.
